language_task: Put the spoon in the drawer.
outcome_evidence: The robot acquires and lifts the spoon in frames 93–120 (left_ego_image, wrist_image), then carries it toward the open drawer. In frames 220–228 (image, wrist_image), the spoon leaves the gripper and falls outside the drawer onto the tabletop. Frames 229–237 (image, left_ego_image) show it remaining on the table, establishing a visibly failed placement rather than merely unconfirmed completion.

failure_annotations.explanation: After successfully carrying the spoon to the drawer, the robot opens its gripper without placing the spoon securely inside. Frames 220–224 (wrist_image, image) show the spoon leaving the fingers and falling outside the drawer; frames 227–228 (image, left_ego_image) show it landing on the tabletop. The visible placement fails; the images do not establish a hidden cause for the misalignment.
failure_annotations.recovery: Reacquire the spoon from the tabletop, align it fully over the drawer interior, lower it inside, and release only after confirming clearance from the rim. No human intervention appears necessary.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The spoon falls onto the table and remains intact, with no visible damage or disruption to unrelated objects.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The spoon remains accessible on the tabletop and the drawer remains open, so another acquisition and placement attempt requires no environmental reset or human intervention.
